beats.narration: Under the Long Night of the Arab yoke comes აბო — a young perfumer of Baghdad, Arab-born, in the company of a Georgian prince returning home. The age is heavy; the Unremembering presses on a city that is told, day by day, to forget its own name. Witness a stranger arrive who will give that city back its memory by his death.

In Kartli, Abo studies the faith of the land that sheltered him and, freely, embraces it — and is baptized. Witness a conviction freely chosen. This is not a tale against the people he was born among, who are not the enemy here; it is a tale of one soul choosing what it will not betray.

Tbilisi's rulers seize Abo and demand he recant and return to the faith of his birth, on pain of death. He refuses — calmly, without contempt for anyone. Witness him hold to the thing he has chosen while the whole weight of the Long Night leans on him to forget it.

They behead Abo, burn his body, and cast the ashes from the Metekhi cliff into the Mtkvari, so that no grave, no relic, no memory of him should remain — the Unremembering's whole purpose in one act. You cannot save his life; that is the truth of the tale. Ward his witness. Stand so that the river does not carry away the memory of what he chose.

Where his ashes fell, a light is seen on the water, and the city — Christian and Muslim both, who knew him — does not forget. Restore the remembrance: Abo becomes the patron of Tbilisi, the proof that even in the Long Night a city kept the memory of a just man against every effort to erase it.

Abo Tbileli stands in the Living Chronicle as the patron of the city that the empires could not make forget. The Long Night did not win. You have kept it — a memory the river was told to swallow, and did not.
